[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]The Sun is a 4.5 billion-year-old yellow dwarf star at the center of our solar system. Made of hydrogen and helium, it lies about 150 million kilometers from Earth.  The Sun provides the energy that makes life possible on Earth.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Mercury is the smallest planet and closest to the Sun, just slightly larger than Earth's Moon. From its surface, the Sun appears over three times larger and up to seven times brighter than from Earth.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Venus is the second planet from the Sun and the closest one to Earth. Often called Earth's twin due to its similar size and composition, it's actually the hottest planet in the solar system.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Earth is the largest of the rocky planets and the only one with surface liquid water. Its name comes from Old English and Germanic, meaning "the ground". Unlike other planets, it’s not named after a Greek or Roman god.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. It is mostly a cold, dusty desert with a thin atmosphere. Mars has different seasons, polar ice caps, extinct volcanoes, canyons, and even weather.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Jupiter is the oldest planet in the solar system, formed 4.6 billion years ago from leftover solar material. It’s also the largest, with enough room to hold a thousand Earths. Surprisingly, it has the shortest day, due to its fast spin rate.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Saturn is a giant planet made mostly of hydrogen and helium. It has the most stunning rings in the solar system and dozens of moons. From Enceladus's water jets to Titan's methane lakes, Saturn's system offers rich opportunities for scientific discoveries.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Uranus is a cold, windy ice giant with 13 faint rings and 28 small moons. Its extreme tilt makes it appear to spin sideways as it orbits the Sun. Discovered in 1781 by William Herschel, it was the first planet found using a telescope.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]

[outline=#000000][lineThickness=2]Neptune is a dark, cold ice giant with supersonic winds, located over 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth. Discovered in 1846, it completed its first full orbit in 2011. Sunlight on Neptune is about 900 times dimmer than on Earth.

[tag=link][color=#9999ff][u]View Source[/u][/tag]
